original.target_description: Study 1: mean moral judgment across six vignettes, cleanliness versus neutral priming in the low response effort subsample (below median survey duration).

n.sample_role: Participants in the final low response effort subsample used in the independent-samples comparison of composite moral judgments.
n.exclusions: Study 1 retained 214 of 268 recruited participants after planned exclusions for hypothesis guessing or insufficient effort responding on moral judgment items. The planned exclusion section reports 2 hypothesis guessers and 54 respondents faster than 675 words/minute on at least two moral vignettes; these counts are not summed because overlap is not specified. The critical subsample comprises retained participants below the median survey duration. End-of-survey quality-control/IER scale exclusions were supplementary, not the primary analysis.

Preregistration explicitly identifies Huang Study 2, whereas supplied original study identifier is Study 1 (measured low response effort).

notes:
Original extraction matches supplied Study 1 low response effort subsample. Replication target mismatch: linked preregistration jqzsf item1 explicitly states "This is  the Low Response Effort condition of study 2 in Huang, 2014." Preregistration cached at /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/d1909c4c66942a0b70c5d591.txt. Replication d is printed in post-completion item30; no exact p is printed there, so p remains null. The preregistered p=0.04, d=-0.29, n=218 describe Huang Study 2 and were not substituted for replication results. Replication n is the authors' post-exclusion count; allocation and test-specific missingness are not documented. No statistics recomputed from raw data. Original exclusion counts may overlap; no count inferred by subtraction.
Completion source review (n_o): The Study 1 Results explicitly identifies n = 107 as the low response effort subsample and immediately reports the cleanliness-versus-neutral composite moral judgment comparison for that subsample. This matches the supplied study and outcome description. Table 1 corroborates the final subgroup counts; the overall retained N = 214 and recruitment N = 268 are not substituted for this target analytic N.
